shortDescription: Microsoft President Brad Smith will oversee the company's communications department, a company spokesperson confirmed on Thursday.

children: Microsoft President Brad Smith will oversee the company's communications department, a company spokesperson confirmed on Thursday.

The change puts Smith, one of Microsoft's most prominent public-facing executives, in charge of corporate communications as the company faces issues ranging from artificial intelligence to regulation.
Smith has become a prominent voice for Microsoft on public policy issues, including AI governance, technology regulation and the geopolitical implications of the company's global expansion.
Brent Colburn, vice president for global public affairs, will serve as interim communications leader during the transition, the spokesperson said.

Smith joined Microsoft in 1993, and in 2002 he was named Microsoft's general counsel, a role in which he spent the next decade leading the company's efforts to resolve antitrust disputes with governments around the world and companies across the technology sector.
